basis: Exactly one open each of the three hash-verified canonical original PNGs; no SVG or previous modern figure inspected.

facts.description: One concave mirror on the right, reflective face toward the left, curved solid edge with short diagonal backing hatches on the right. One solid horizontal principal axis crosses O, F, P in that left-to-right order.

Six source letter labels: O (left axis point), F (axis point on dashed plane), P (mirror vertex on axis), D (above F on dashed plane), C (upper mirror intersection on the secondary axis), K (mirror intersection horizontally right of D). A fourth, unlettered mirror hit lies below P. No numerical values or measured scale.

A single vertical dashed line through D and F extends both above and below the ray fan. Its vertical Chinese label names the focal plane. It is perpendicular to the shared horizontal axis; this is not a second panel.
The oblique solid line through O, D, C is both the secondary-axis direction and the retraced upper ray path. It continues down-left of O.

Four solid incident ray paths run up-right from the lower-left to C, K, P, and the unlettered lower hit, respectively. They are parallel to the O-D-C direction. The K-bound incident path passes F. Arrowheads on the incident branches point toward the mirror.

Four solid reflected paths from those mirror hits pass through D and continue away on the left. The C branch retraces the O-D-C line down-left. The K branch goes horizontally left through D. The P branch goes up-left through D; the lower-hit branch goes more steeply up-left through D. Reflected arrowheads point away from the mirror. Crossings away from lettered points are unmarked crossings, not new labelled points.

No grid, tick scale, extra plane, separate subfigure, dashed optical ray, screen, source apparatus, or arbitrary-angle exact focusing claim is present. The printed 144 is a figure identifier, not data.

modernClarifications: Translate the focal-plane label to English.

Retain all ray/point incidences in one shared frame while regularizing the sketch to a narrow, small-angle bundle. The drawn common point is an idealized paraxial construction, not exact spherical reflection for an arbitrary aperture.

Use a circular mirror centered at O. Select the F/D/K layout in the approximate focal construction so the source's K-D horizontal branch and F-K incident line remain represented; do not assert exact half-radius focal length or equal arbitrary-angle distances.
Add the English scope label Paraxial model, separately from source facts. No newly visible name is added to the unlettered lower hit.

facts.description: One front-view circular optical disk with a circular rim. Large dark inward triangular graduation marks surround the circumference; shorter marks lie between them. The source has no readable angle numbers. Dense horizontal marks across the disk are apparatus surface shading/ruling, not an explicitly dimensioned graph or rectangular cell grid.

A vertical stem exits the bottom rim. A top assembly includes a dark knob, narrow threaded/spring-like vertical neck, widening angular clamp housing, visible small fastener holes, and a connector meeting the top rim. A dark horizontal curved mirror/mount occupies the center region, with visible end fasteners.

Low-contrast pale narrow traces occupy the upper half of the disk and approach the central mirror assembly. Some traces appear nearly vertical and others oblique. The single open does not resolve every incident/reflected trace, its endpoints, or its relationship to the curved reflective face with sufficient confidence for a complete source inventory. No clearly printed ray arrowheads, named points, F/O/P labels, principal-axis label, focal plane, virtual-focus dot, or dashed virtual extension is present.

facts.description: One convex mirror on the left-middle, bulging toward incoming light from the left; solid curved edge, diagonal backing hatches on its right. One solid horizontal principal axis passes P at the mirror vertex, F behind the mirror, and O farther right, in that order.

Three source labels P, F, O. F and O have point marks; P is at the vertex/central ray. Six unlettered off-axis mirror hits accompany the central vertex hit. No numerical values, measured ticks, focal plane, or extra subpanel.

Seven solid horizontal incident paths from the left, including the central path on the axis, reach seven mirror positions. Incident arrowheads point right toward the mirror. The six side paths occur three above and three below the central axis.

Seven solid reflected paths travel left away from the mirror. Three upper side paths diverge up-left and three lower side paths diverge down-left. The central path returns left along the axis. Reflected arrowheads point away from the mirror. Incidence and reflection share mirror hits; optical paths crossing elsewhere do not introduce labelled points.

Six dashed backward extensions run from the off-axis mirror hits to the F mark behind the mirror. The central supporting line is the solid axis rather than an extra dashed line. The dashed parts have no propagation arrowhead to the right of the mirror. Solid reflected light is not drawn continuing to F or O.
No convergence screen, real ray through the mirror, plane, dashed incident branch, exact arbitrary-ray claim, or additional named point. The printed figure identifier is not a measured quantity.

modernClarifications: Use a deterministic circular convex mirror centered at O and an idealized paraxial virtual-focus construction. Exact straight-line concurrence in this schematic is not an assertion that exact spherical reflection converges for arbitrary rays.
Keep seven physical ray paths and six nonpropagating dashed extensions. All solid physical rays terminate at/reflect from the mirror; no rightward physical arrow is added behind it.
Retain English letter labels P, F, O, and add Paraxial model only as a scope clarification, not original content.
